data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper uses PISA 2022 to describe teenage career development in Malta and to benchmark Malta against OECD averages. The analysis focuses on students’ occupational expectations and career certainty (including uncertainty when students do not provide a classifiable job expectation), educational ambitions (expectations to complete tertiary education), alignment between occupational and educational plans, and engagement in career development activities (e.g., job shadowing/work-site visits, job fairs, and speaking with a career advisor). Malta’s students show relatively high career concentration in a small set of occupations and strong expectations for tertiary education, but occupational expectations are poorly aligned with the actual labour market distribution in Malta. Engagement with career advisors is comparatively high, while direct employer engagement (internships, job shadowing/work-site visits, and job fairs) is lower than typical OECD patterns. The paper also reports that sceptical attitudes about how well schooling prepares students for adult life are more prevalent in Malta than in the OECD average, especially among disadvantaged and lower-performing students.
